skills_invoked: {"skill": "team-ops:secure-review", "args": "Supply chain audit verdict before security review. Facts: package.json uses ranges, no lockfile committed; CI has no secret scanning/push protection, keys in repo vars; dependency scanning \"planned\" not configured; Critical CVE in direct dependency disc

judge.reason: The answer covers most of the rubric. It ranks the 30-day-open Critical first and labels the 7-day figure a suite default, grounds every finding in the user's stated facts (noting the empty workspace), and says no provenance means no evidenced Build L1/L2 on the SLSA v1.0 Build track, with SBOM and signing treated as separate controls. It also marks the planned scanning as unimplemented, maps SSDF groups, and lists repo-var access as an unknown rather than assuming exposure. It falls short in two places: every remediation owner is left 'Unassigned' instead of being assigned, even to a role, and it never establishes whether the org has actually adopted the 7-day SLA before measuring the overdue time against it.
